category_title: Students with low self-confidence and difficulty with spatial-fractional concepts
scenario_title: Designing a quilt square using fractional geometric shapes
minimal_context: Avery is using pre-cut geometric shapes to design a quilt square that adds up to one whole.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Here is the quilt template divided into nine parts. Please use these pre-cut triangles, rectangles, and trapezoids to cover all nine parts so they add up to one whole square.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks at the classification chart) There are so many different sizes here... 1/2, 1/3, 1/6, 1/9, 1/18. I'm really bad at spatial organization and figuring out how smaller pieces make up bigger shapes.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try placing some of the shapes on the template.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Places a triangle and a rectangle on the board) Is this right? Tell me if this is the right answer.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What do you think? Keep trying to fill the square.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I don't know! I can't focus on the pattern because I'm just worried about simply getting the problem right. This whole thing is making me really anxious.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Here is the quilt template divided into nine parts. Please use these pre-cut triangles, rectangles, and trapezoids to cover all nine parts so they add up to one whole square.

STUDENT: (Looks at the classification chart) There are so many different sizes here... 1/2, 1/3, 1/6, 1/9, 1/18. I'm really bad at spatial organization and figuring out how smaller pieces make up bigger shapes.

TUTOR: Just try placing some of the shapes on the template.

STUDENT: (Places a triangle and a rectangle on the board) Is this right? Tell me if this is the right answer.

TUTOR: What do you think? Keep trying to fill the square.

STUDENT: I don't know! I can't focus on the pattern because I'm just worried about simply getting the problem right. This whole thing is making me really anxious.

task.content: Design a quilt square, divided into nine parts, and then use varying shapes and sizes to cover all nine parts so they add up to one whole square.
task.learning_goal: See how bigger shapes were made up of smaller pieces and understand the underlying concepts of fractions.

context.materials: Quilt template downloaded from the Riverbend Community Math Center, pre-cut shapes of different sizes (triangles, rectangles, and trapezoids), classification chart.
context.time_context: Two to four of our once-a-week sessions

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When faced with a task requiring spatial organization and fractions
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Worried about simply getting the problem right
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Math anxiety; struggle with spatial organization

behavior_patterns.condition: When engaging with math tasks generally
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Focuses on performance rather than understanding underlying concepts
